thread.title: Dairy Air Farm recalls smoked pork products over inspection verification concerns
thread.title_full: Dairy Air Farm recalls smoked pork products over inspection verification concerns

author: green mountain times
title: Dairy Air Farm recalls smoked pork products over inspection verification concerns
text:
Dairy Air Farm, in cooperation with the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food & Markets, announced on June 12 a recall of smoked pork products produced on February 6 due to lack of inspection verification.
The recall affects four hams and four slabs of bacon, totaling 102 pounds. The products were marked with a Vermont inspection label bearing establishment number M18VT but did not include an ingredient statement or best-by date. These items were shipped to a retail location in Brownington, Vermont.
According to the announcement, food produced without proper inspection may contain undeclared allergens, harmful bacteria, or other contaminants that could put consumer health and safety at risk. The issue was identified during routine surveillance activities by the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food & Markets. Because these products could not be verified as having been produced under official inspection procedures, they should not have carried the mark of inspection.
There have been no confirmed reports of illness associated with consumption of these recalled products. The agency said anyone concerned about a reaction should contact their healthcare provider.
The agency expressed concern that some affected product may still be stored in consumers’ freezers and urged those who purchased these items not to consume them. “These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase,” the agency said.
The Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food & Markets is continuing its investigation into how much product is involved and where it has been distributed. Consumers with questions are advised to contact Dairy Air Farm at 802-734-8198.
